plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: A fragrant evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and dense spikes of small tubular flowers. Widely cultivated in gardens and commercial fields, it is a favorite of bees and butterflies and is prized for its essential oil.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (June through August in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Tasmania, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because the Romans used lavender to scent their baths.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: A hardy perennial of the daisy family with drooping pink-purple petals around a prominent spiky, orange-brown central cone. It thrives in prairies, open woodlands, and sunny gardens and attracts pollinators and goldfinches.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall (June through September)
plants.location: Native to central and eastern North America; widely grown in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: The genus name comes from the Greek 'echinos', meaning hedgehog, a reference to the spiky central cone.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large round leaves held above the water and spectacular flowers on tall stalks. Its flowers open in the morning and close at night, and its leaves are famously water-repellent.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer (June through August in temperate Asia; monsoon season in the tropics)
plants.location: Native to Asia and northern Australia; grown in ponds and wetlands in India, China, Japan, Vietnam, and elsewhere
plants.funFact: Lotus seeds have been germinated after more than 1,000 years of dormancy, and the flower can regulate its own temperature to about 30-35°C.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub producing the largest flower head of the protea family, up to 30 cm across, with a central cluster of flowers surrounded by colorful bracts. It grows in the fynbos vegetation of the Cape region and blooms in the Southern Hemisphere's winter and spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through spring in the Southern Hemisphere, with peak bloom from winter to early spring (May to September)
plants.location: Native to the Western and Eastern Cape of South Africa; cultivated in Australia, Hawaii, and California
plants.funFact: It is the national flower of South Africa, and the protea family is so ancient that it dates back to when the supercontinent Gondwana still existed.
